subject.title: [Refactor] Extract canonical configuration validation from core to plugin boundaries

question: Does current main still contain a specific plugin-owned configuration schema that should move behind the existing manifest validation contract, or should this broad refactor be closed as already architecturally covered?
rationale: The desired ownership boundary matches repository direction, but current documentation and validation seams already implement that boundary; only maintainers can confirm whether a residual schema is intentional core policy or misplaced plugin policy.

options.title: Narrow to a residual schema
options.body: Identify each concrete core-owned plugin schema and approve a bounded ownership move with startup and compatibility coverage.

options.title: Close as architecturally covered
options.body: Close the issue if the cited schemas are generic core contracts or already supplied through plugin manifests.

options.title: Authorize a coordinated redesign
options.body: Approve broader dynamic composition only with an explicit compatibility plan for startup, unavailable plugins, and generated schema consumers.

recommendation.title: Narrow to a residual schema
recommendation.body: Identify each concrete core-owned plugin schema and approve a bounded ownership move with startup and compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal connects this person to the original manifest validation contract and its intended ownership boundary.
